# Alert configuration

The MVP configuration, locked from the backtest. The guiding principle: **fire
broadly for recall (misses are costly), escalate by magnitude/extent, and never let
a magnitude criterion *suppress* a flag.**

```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_parquet("../data/seas5_admin_drought_alerts_2026-06.parquet")   # adm0, issued June 2026
ev = df[df.state == "evaluable"]
```

## Evaluability (where we'll judge at all)

A unit × season is assessed only with enough *trusted* ground — by **fraction OR
absolute area**, so large countries aren't withheld for a modest percentage:

- in-season (PSP) coverage ≥ 10%, **and**
- in-season ∧ skilled coverage ≥ 25% **OR** ≥ 25,000 km² absolute.

## Drought alert

- **WATCH** — fires on the dry event alone: forecast **dry RP ≥ 3** (below-normal).
  Recall-optimized.
- **ALERT** — escalates a watch when severe/widespread; **any** of these triggers
  it (OR — escalation never suppresses a watch):
  `z ≤ −1.5` **OR** `dry_frac_footprint ≥ 0.80` **OR** `dry_area_km2 ≥ 300,000`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-counts
pd.DataFrame({
    "evaluable": [len(ev)],
    "drought_watch": [(df.drought_tier == "watch").sum()],
    "drought_alert": [(df.drought_tier == "alert").sum()],
    "flood_watch": [(df.flood_tier == "watch").sum()],
})
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-top-alerts
#| fig-cap: "Largest drought alerts by forecast dry area (issued June 2026)."
(df[df.drought_tier == "alert"]
   .sort_values("dry_area_km2", ascending=False)
   [["admin", "season", "dry_rp", "z", "dry_frac_footprint", "dry_area_km2"]]
   .head(20).reset_index(drop=True))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Escalation thresholds are backtest-calibrated
The escalation arms are calibrated as a **precision lever** by a per-year backtest
(`backtest_verify.py` §D): within the fired (watch) universe — 6,787 unit×year cases —
each arm is scored against the **observed** severe drought (ERA5 dry RP ≥ 5). The base
severe rate among watches is 0.33.

- `z ≤ −1.5` is the strongest arm (alert precision 0.46, **lift 1.42** over base).
- The original extent bars were far too loose: `dry_frac ≥ 0.50` was nearly implied by
  firing (median `dry_frac` among fired ≈ 0.87) and `dry_area ≥ 100,000` mostly just
  escalated large countries. Together they escalated **>50%** of watches on a
  climatological average — the inverted split.
- Tightening them to `dry_frac ≥ 0.80` / `dry_area ≥ 300,000` restores a watch-heavy
  ~**2:1** split (alert share 0.51 → 0.32) and raises alert precision (lift 1.17 → 1.26),
  with `z` left unchanged (it was never the problem).

A broadly dry *forecast year* like 2026 still fires many alerts — that is the severity
signal, not a miscalibration. The split is calibrated on climatology, not tuned to make
any single year watch-heavy.
:::

## A continuous product: return period per unit (no threshold)

The pipeline computes the **exact dry return period, percentile, and z for every
evaluable unit** — the tiers are just a threshold on top. So a no-threshold
*return-period map* is a first-class product from the same table, useful on its own.
Admin geometries come from the ASAP FC exported once (`export_admin_boundaries.py`),
joined to the alert table on `asap0_id`; Natural Earth 110m provides the neutral
basemap (grey = not evaluable / not in season).

```{python}
#| label: fig-rp-map
#| fig-cap: "Forecast dry return period per country, by forecastable season (issued June 2026). Grey = not evaluable / not in season. The continuous, no-threshold product."
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import geopandas as gpd
ne = gpd.read_file("../data/boundaries/naturalearth_admin0.geojson")
adm0 = gpd.read_file("../data/boundaries/asap_adm0.geojson")
SEASONS = ["JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(13, 9))
axes = axes.ravel()
for ax, s in zip(axes, SEASONS):
    ne.plot(ax=ax, color="#eeeeee", ec="white", lw=0.15)
    sub = df[(df.season == s) & (df.state == "evaluable")][["asap0_id", "dry_rp"]]
    g = adm0.merge(sub, on="asap0_id").dropna(subset=["dry_rp"])
    if len(g):
        g.plot(ax=ax, column="dry_rp", cmap="YlOrRd", vmin=1, vmax=10, ec="#999999", lw=0.1)
    ax.set_xlim(-180, 180); ax.set_ylim(-60, 84); ax.set_axis_off(); ax.set_title(s, fontsize=10)
sm = mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap="YlOrRd", norm=mpl.colors.Normalize(1, 10))
axes[-1].set_axis_off()
fig.colorbar(sm, ax=axes[-1], fraction=0.5, label="dry RP (years)")
fig.suptitle("Forecast dry return period by season — issued June 2026", y=1.0)
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

The same map at adm1 (finer units) uses `asap_adm1.geojson`, joined on `asap1_id`.
Its distribution across evaluable units:

```{python}
#| label: fig-rp-dist
#| fig-cap: "Forecast dry return period across evaluable adm0 units (issued June 2026)."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.0))
ax.hist(ev.dry_rp.dropna(), bins=range(1, 36, 2), edgecolor="white")
ax.set_xlabel("forecast dry return period (years)"); ax.set_ylabel("adm0 × season units")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Flood alert (caveated)

A wet-tail analogue — **FLOOD WATCH** fires on wet **RP ≥ 3**.

::: {.callout-important}
## Flood here is unvalidated and weak
Seasonal cumulative precipitation is a poor flood proxy — floods are driven by
sub-seasonal intensity and antecedent conditions a 3-month mean cannot see. Unlike
the drought rule, the flood flag is **not backtested**. It is provided as a
structural placeholder, to be treated as a coarse wetness indicator, not a trigger.
:::
